chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Scarcity of recording and the rise of ballrooms
summary: Little recording went on before the big-band cycle, which moved bands from night clubs into ballrooms and society clubs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: They was working two or three, you know -- that was before a lot of recording came in.
It was a little -- some recording

around, but not that much. So they weren't doing too much recording (inaudible).
If you record, maybe a whole band would record, or something like that. You didn't have too many small bands recording.
When (inaudible) we got into the small bands. That didn't come later. That came later after the big band circle, you know.

This was (inaudible) what a big band -- You must remember, after the Wall Street crash, this was a cycle where the big bands were really coming back from out of the night clubs going into the dance area.
Ballrooms. Savoy Ballroom and the R. Hammer -- they would take it over. They were private clubs.
You had a lot of private clubs that could keep a ballroom going around the clock, you know.
So, people were going out in the clubs, you know, different society clubs; and things like that.
